title: Forensic usage log retention and access-control playbook for billing audits
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: produce a defensible, operational playbook and technical implementation for long-term, tamper-evident retention of billing-related usage events and controlled investigator access for SOC/financial audits. This ticket covers schema, retention tiers, immutable storage, access controls, export formats, and verification tooling.
scope:
1) Define canonical billing event schema (ingest-time fields, sequence number, source, model_id, route, tokens_in/tokens_out, cost_unit, tenant_id, rate_limit_bucket_id).
2) Retention policy: hot (90d) for fast reconciliation, warm (1 year) for monthly/yearly audits, cold/archival (7 years) for financial compliance and legal hold.
3) Tamper-evidence: append-only writes with checksums and write-ahead log (WAL) snapshots; store daily manifests signed by KMS.
4) Access controls: RBAC + SSO (SCIM provisioning), emergency access workflow with approval audit trail.
5) Export and verification: reproducible CSV/Parquet exports, reconciliation scripts, and sample Kibana/Grafana queries for auditors.
6) Forensics playbook sections: incident collection, freeze-copy, hash verification, and chain-of-custody notes for legal teams.
acceptance_criteria:
- Canonical schema document published and approved by PM/Finance.
- Durable store configured (S3 glacier + object lock or equivalent) with lifecycle transitions matching policy.
- Daily manifest generation with KMS signatures and a sample verifier script in repo.
- RBAC roles and SCIM group mapping documented and tested (no cross-tenant access).
- End-to-end test demonstrating: simulated usage stream -> stored events -> export -> reconciliation matches billing records within defined tolerance.
- Runbook for auditors and SOC containing sample queries and evidence checklist.

engineering_notes:
Key trade-offs:
- Using S3 Object Lock + Glacier for long retention minimizes infra cost but adds retrieval latency for auditor requests; we propose pre-approved on-demand retrieval SLA (48h) for SOC evidence.
- Immutable logs require key isolation; key escrow increases operational overhead but provides strong tamper-resistance for legal audits.
- To correlate rate-limit/quotas with billing we must emit deterministic quota_bucket ids at ingress; this requires changing rate limiter to attach bucket metadata to every usage event.
Operational steps: implement schema -> wire into ingress producer -> store manifests -> nightly reconciliation -> provide auditor exports + verifier script.
risks:
- Clock skew across producers could reorder events and complicate sequence verification; mitigated by monotonic sequence numbers per-tenant plus ingest timestamp.
- Large customers with high retention needs may incur significant storage costs; finance to propose cost allocation or alternative retention tiers.
- Emergency access process must be auditable and cannot grant write/delete rights to logs.
